newsitem.title: USA: First lady says White House plan to aid D.C. coming.
newsitem.headline: First lady says White House plan to aid D.C. coming.

text.p: The White House will soon announce a major package of initiatives to help bring the nation's capital out of its deep financial crisis, Hillary Rodham Clinton told The Washington Post.

In an interview published on Saturday, the first lady told the Post, "In the next few weeks, some of the administration's plans and commitments will be unveiled ... I believe that, as the president has said, the District is in a difficult political and legal situation, and the financial strains on the District have to be addressed."

The District of Columbia has been financially strapped for years, and late last year the city's congressionally mandated financial control board ordered city officials to cut $85 million in projected overspending in 1997.

The control board earlier released a plan for the city that implored the United States government to take over $1 billion annually in District programs that in most other U.S. jurisdications are financed by states, including Medicaid.

President Clinton said on Dec. 13 that he agreed that the city cannot afford to pay for so many state functions and pledged a "systematic effort" to help. He is set to announce details in his FY'98 proposed federal budget in February.

In the Post interview, Mrs. Clinton said the White House plan will deal with political as well as financial issues. D.C. control board Chairman Andrew Brimmer said he will meet with Office of Management and Budget (OMB) director Franklin Raines next week to review the plan.

Sources told Reuters on Friday that the OMB is recommending the federal government take over some of the costs of the city's estimated $5 billion unfunded pension liability. The pension plan problem costs the city hundreds of millions of dollars annually and Brimmer has warned it could have a "catastrophic" impact on the city.
The OMB is also recommending that the federal government pay more of the District of Columbia's Medicaid bills and assume prison costs for city felons, sources said.
In return, the city would forfeit an annual $660 million payment it gets from Congress to offset what it loses from tax-exempt federal properties, sources said.

Currently, the District and U.S. government each pay 50 percent of Medicaid reimbursement costs for D.C. citizens. Sources told Reuters the OMB will recommend the federal share be hiked, but not by how much.

On prisons, the government would assume the costs of imprisoning D.C. felons, but it was not clear whether the federal government would ship prisoners to other federal jails, or use existing city facililties.
The Post also said the administration is working on a tax incentive program to spur job creation and investment in the District.

White House spokesman Michael McCurry on Friday described as "speculation" a Wall Street Journal report that the Clinton Administration soon will unveil an aid package for D.C., but he said there would be more details of the plan in the upcoming federal budget announcement.
